question: What is the main goal of using assistive devices for patients?

options.A: To completely replace the need for nursing staff
options.B: To maintain or improve functional independence

explanation: You got this! Assistive tools are specially made to help patients do daily tasks on their own and build up their confidence. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h1)

question: How do assistive devices help a busy bedside nurse?

options.A: They eliminate all risks associated with patient handling
options.B: They bridge the gap between dependency and safe self-care
options.C: They complicate basic physical assessments unnecessarily
options.D: They transfer total legal liability to the equipment manufacturer

explanation: Well done! These tools support your nursing care by helping patients move safely while encouraging them to do as much as they can for themselves. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which tool is best for reducing friction when moving a bedridden patient up in bed?
explanation: Spot on! Slide sheets are made of slick material that cuts down on friction and shearing, making repositioning easier on both you and the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h2)

question: A patient with complete paralysis in both legs needs to move from the bed to a chair. What is the safest equipment to use?
explanation: Correct! Since the patient cannot bear weight, belts or walkers won't work safely. A mechanical lift is essential here to protect everyone. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the main feature that sets an automated wheelchair apart from a regular manual one?

options.A: An integrated electronic health record terminal
options.D: Computerized navigation and alternative control interfaces

explanation: You nailed it! Automated wheelchairs use smart tech and alternative controls for patients who cannot push standard manual wheels. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why are powered exoskeletons so helpful in neurological rehabilitation?

options.A: They facilitate repetitive, computer-guided gait training
options.B: They permanently repair damaged central nervous tissue
options.C: They eliminate the need for physical therapy supervision entirely
options.D: They replace the metabolic functions of lower limb muscles

explanation: Great job! Exoskeletons help the brain and nerves heal by guiding patients through steady, repeated walking movements. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of linking smart assistive devices directly to the Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: Complete elimination of nursing care plans
options.B: Automatic prescription of new mobility medications
options.C: Instant replacement of broken hospital equipment
options.D: Real-time transmission of patient activity data

explanation: Spot on! Direct linking means device usage and activity stats flow straight into digital records without you having to type everything out manually. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h4)

question: How do smart bed sensors help keep patients safe in the ward?

options.A: They diagnose the underlying cause of patient agitation
options.B: They adjust room temperature based on the patient's body heat
options.C: They automatically administer pain medication when restlessness occurs
options.D: They trigger automated alerts when an unassisted exit is attempted

explanation: Correct! Bed sensors link to the nurse call alarm to warn you before a fall-risk patient tries to get out of bed alone. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h4)

question: What should a nurse do first before picking out a mobility device for a patient?

options.B: Order the most expensive model available
options.C: Document the discharge summary in the EHR
options.D: Request permission from the hospital director

explanation: You got it! Checking the patient's physical and mental status first ensures you pick the right tool for their unique needs. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h5)

question: A patient gets a new walking frame but looks confused about how to use it. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Leave the device at the bedside for trial and error
options.B: Document that the patient is entirely non-compliant
options.C: Remove the device and insist the patient remains in bed
options.D: Provide clear instruction and supervise initial practice

explanation: Wonderful! Teaching patients step-by-step and watching them practice builds safety and trust before they try moving alone. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is a major ethical worry when using continuous smart monitoring devices on patients?

options.A: Mandatory reduction of nursing staffing numbers
options.B: Guaranteed elimination of all hospital financial costs
options.C: Potential infringement on patient privacy and dignity
options.D: Automatic loss of patient health insurance coverage

explanation: Spot on! Constant digital tracking can sometimes cross the line and conflict with a patient's right to personal privacy. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why is it often hard for everyone to access advanced assistive technology in healthcare?

options.A: Manufacturers prohibit developing countries from purchasing items
options.B: High costs can limit availability for vulnerable populations
options.C: Patients universally reject digital tools in favor of manual care
options.D: Advanced devices cannot function in tropical climates

explanation: Correct! High-tech robotics and smart gear are often too expensive for underfunded health systems and everyday patients. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T4#GNS113_U4_T4_h6)
